description: React Loadly gives React and Next.js apps accessible loading UI: 30+ spinners/loaders, Skeletonize (turns your real component into its skeleton), SkeletonLoader and SkeletonGroupLoader for skeleton screens, SkeletonSwitchLoader for loading/error/empty switching, and loading-state hooks. TypeScript, SSR-friendly, ARIA role="status", reduced-motion support.
rules: To skeleton an existing component, wrap it: `<Skeletonize loading={isLoading}><UserCard user={data ?? placeholderUser} /></Skeletonize>`. Pass realistic placeholder data while loading; the real component renders and its text, images, icons and controls become skeleton blocks. Do not write a separate skeleton layout for a component you can wrap.
For skeletons of UI that does not exist yet (e.g. a page shell), use explicit `SkeletonLoader` + `SkeletonGroupLoader`. `AutoSkeletonLoader` is deprecated and will be removed in v4; do not use it.
`Skeletonize` props: `loading`, `animation`, `baseColor`, `highlightColor`, `speed`, `loadingLabel`, `as`. Add `data-skeleton` to an element that should also become a block.
Import the stylesheet once in the app root: `import "react-loadly/styles.css"` (or wrap the app with `<LoadlyProvider>`, which injects styles).
Components use React context and hooks, so in Next.js App Router use them from files that start with "use client" (or pass them as client-component fallbacks).
Always set a meaningful `aria-label` such as "Loading orders".
